principles: Preserve the existing workflow CLI trust boundary; ordinary koala evidence remains local or transport-only unless server receipt verification exists.
Introduce authority-enforce capability as an isolated opt-in subsystem, not a global CLI role change.
Mechanically test anti-overclaim behavior before adding any runner execution capability.
Keep Mac Runner and Python authority roles explicit so future agents do not treat colocation or naming as authority.
drivers: Existing PD-1 docs currently defer enforce-mode CLI authority work until a product decision exists.
User wants a path to headless/CI authority execution without weakening anti-forgery guarantees.
Milestone 0 must be safe to merge before actor keys, job claim, provider execution, full envelopes, and receipt verification are implemented.

options.name: A: mutate ordinary koala into enforce authority client
pros: Potentially faster direct integration with existing authority-submit code
cons: Expands the trusted computing base too far
Risks local/shadow evidence being misread as production authority
Conflicts with the PD-1 thin-client boundary

options.name: B: add isolated koala authority enforce subsystem
pros: Keeps workflow CLI and production runner authority separate
Allows headless/CI runner work to progress with explicit opt-in
Lets tests enforce that ordinary local/shadow evidence is still not L2+
cons: Requires a little more command/catalog design
Later milestones must bridge policy discovery, actor keys, jobs, envelopes, and receipts carefully

options.name: C: do nothing until Mac Runner covers all headless scenarios
cons: Does not address CI/Linux/no-UI use cases
Leaves the product decision unresolved and future agents will keep re-opening the same discussion

chosen: B: add isolated koala authority enforce subsystem
rationale: Choose an isolated authority-enforce subsystem because it gives the user a path to headless production authority while preserving the existing anti-forgery trust boundary for ordinary Koala workflow commands.

preMortem.scenario: Future agent claims ordinary koala verification_evidence_add is now production L2+ because PD-2 mentions enforce mode.
preMortem.trigger: Docs use broad wording like Koala CLI is authority-capable without isolating the enforce namespace.
preMortem.consequence: Local JSON or accepted true transport results can be mistaken for server-backed authority evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: PD-2 wording must separate ordinary koala workflow client from future koala authority enforce runner, and boundary smoke tests must keep thin transport classification distinct from receipt-backed L2+.

preMortem.scenario: Milestone 0 accidentally implements partial runner behavior without actor key or receipt verification.
preMortem.trigger: A command placeholder submits evidence or reuses existing authority-submit enforce mode as if it were production authority.
preMortem.consequence: The system gains a confusing half-authority path that can fail open or mislead future reviewers.
preMortem.mitigation: Milestone 0 is limited to docs and classification tests; actor key, job claim, provider execution, full envelope, and receipt verification are explicitly forbidden until later stories.

preMortem.scenario: The new subsystem is treated as replacing Mac Runner.
preMortem.trigger: Docs say CLI runner is canonical or omit Mac Runner from the role table.
preMortem.consequence: Mac-side live E2E and actor-key responsibilities become ambiguous, increasing cross-end drift.
preMortem.mitigation: PD-2 must say Mac Runner remains an execution plane and Python authority remains the receipt authority; TS enforce runner is an additional headless path only.

preMortem.scenario: Tests pass while the important anti-overclaim path is untested.
preMortem.trigger: Only happy-path complete envelope fixtures are added, with no accepted true/no receipt or same-run negative fixture.
preMortem.consequence: Regression can reclassify weak or self-verified evidence as L2+ later.
preMortem.mitigation: Add happy, edge, and adversarial boundary fixtures: complete signed+receipt case, accepted-without-receipt case, same-run/missing-signature cases.
